title: Trapping Rain Water
statement:
You are given `n` non-negative integers describing an elevation map. The `i`-th value is the height of a bar of width 1 standing at position `i`. After it rains, water collects in the dips between bars.

The water above position `i` rises to the lower of two levels: the tallest bar at or to the left of `i`, and the tallest bar at or to the right of `i`. The amount held above that position is this level minus the height of the bar at `i`. Water that would run off beyond the first or last bar is lost.

Compute the total number of units of water that remain on the map. (In interviews this problem is also asked as "snowpack": how many units of snow are captured between the hills.)
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers, the heights.
outputFormat: Print a single integer: the total units of water trapped.

examples.explanation: Water per position, left to right: 0, 0, 0, 3, 2, 1, 3, 0, 1, 3, 0, 0. These add up to 13 units.
Positions 1, 2 and 3 are bounded on the left by a bar of height 3, giving 3, 1 and 3 units. Position 5 has nothing taller on its right, so it holds nothing. Total 7.
Heights only increase, so water at any position would spill to the left. Nothing is trapped.

hints: Focus on a single position: how much water it holds depends only on the tallest bar to its left and the tallest bar to its right.
Precomputing prefix and suffix maximum arrays gives an O(n) time, O(n) space solution.
Two pointers moving inward remove the extra arrays: always advance the side whose current bar is lower, because that side's water level is already decided by its own running maximum.
